A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Regression Trees Know Calculus by Nathan Wycoff. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting and revisions.

before.justification: V3 reports original rotation-prediction experiments, synthetic active-subspace comparisons, MNIST interpretations, and NHEFS analysis in Section 5 and the appendices.

after.justification: V4 retains these empirical studies and adds direct gradient-quality experiments and noise/correlation analyses in Appendix C.1–C.4.

M1.justification: Equation 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same child-mean difference estimator, inherited gradient updates, and Monte Carlo/partition integration procedures. Revised notation, additional explanations, and the altered theoretical splitting assumptions do not establish a change to the proposed estimator.

E1.justification: Coverage expands within synthetic studies through logarithmic, Levy, and Ackley test functions and explicit noisy-output and correlated-input scenarios (Appendix C.1–C.4). The eight prediction datasets, MNIST subsets, and NHEFS application remain.

E2.justification: Figure 10 adds a direct gradient-error comparison against GP, alongside the proposed-method curve labeled Forest. The retained rotation comparisons keep Id/PCA/Rand, and the active-subspace comparisons retain their respective GP/PRA/DASM comparator sets.

E3.justification: New appendix protocols include depth-4/12 and 25%/100% gradient-density controls, gradient L2 error versus runtime, Gaussian noise with standard deviation 0.1, and a correlation sweep evaluated at 100 points. These supplement the retained experiments; their existing cross-validation and model settings are not reported as revised.

E4.justification: Appendix C.1–C.4 substantially expands validation: gradient accuracy versus depth, sample size, dimension and sparsity; direct GP comparison; noisy active-subspace estimation; and sensitivity to input correlation. The earlier classification analysis remains as C.5, with its plotted evidence replaced.

E5.justification: The 20 repetitions documented in Appendix B.2 and the confidence-interval-overlap practice remain unchanged. V4’s checklist restates that significance practice without adding seed counts, interval definitions, or new statistical procedures.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained main figures preserve their displayed results. New Figures 9–12 report gradient accuracy, runtime trade-offs, noise results, and degradation at correlation 0.99. V3’s classification Figure 9 duplicates its regression boxplots; v4’s Figure 13 replaces these with distinct classification Brier-score distributions.

T1.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A replace the gradient convergence analysis: v3’s example rate sqrt(P log N/N) becomes O_P(P/log N) under a different depth schedule. V4 introduces bounded-Hessian and probabilistic cell-width conditions, develops cyclic median-splitting arguments, and revises integral-consistency assumptions. V3’s greedy linear-function thresholding derivation in A.2 is removed.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: extracting tree gradients, enabling gradient-based interpretation, and obtaining useful active-subspace estimates. The added evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly acknowledges that its theory excludes ordinary supervised CART splitting and interprets the slower rate as favoring coarse estimates with abundant data. It adds warnings about poorly sampled input regions, interpretation of correlation sensitivity, and a possible explanation involving overwritten gradient estimates. The removed greedy-splitting analysis also weakens the theoretical support previously offered for sparsity behavior.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies the matrix-square-root transformation used for TBAS rotation, supplies settings for the added synthetic experiments, and states in the checklist that reproduction code and a README are provided. Existing software, hardware, dataset information, and main-experiment runtime disclosures largely remain.

R1.justification: New Section 2.3 connects variable importance with sensitivity analysis through Antoniadis et al., Vannucci et al., and Elie-Dit-Cosaque and Maume-Deschamps. Additional citations contextualize simplified tree theory and sensitivity-based rotation, without substantially redefining the principal novelty claim.

P1.justification: The mathematical exposition is substantially revised through clearer notation in Section 3, rewritten explanation in Section 4, and reorganized assumptions and proofs in Appendix A. Appendix C becomes a multi-section supplement, and a conference checklist is added, although the main six-section narrative remains recognizable.

P2.justification: V4 replaces the two-column main-text format with a single-column conference layout, extensively resizing and relocating retained displays. It adds four experimental figures, replaces the duplicated classification plots, rearranges the MNIST panels, and corrects the directional wording in Figure 7’s caption.

improvement.justification: V4 addresses important weaknesses through a more explicit and restricted convergence analysis, direct gradient-quality and robustness evidence, and replacement of the duplicated classification figure. These substantially improve scope calibration and empirical support despite unchanged headline benchmark scores. Removing the greedy-splitting derivation reduces formal coverage, but the remaining gap between the theory and supervised CART is now clearly acknowledged.
